subject: Post-call: PaceHealth model suitability & quant plan
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Ellie Shaw <ellie@pacehealth.ai>, PaceHealth Platform <infra@pacehealth.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-22T15:05:00Z
Subject: Post-call: PaceHealth model suitability & quant plan

Hi Ellie / PaceHealth infra team —

Thanks again for the demo and the deep dive this morning. Quick recap and a proposed next-step plan so we can align on a short, measurable eval that answers your throughput and quality thresholds.

Call summary (high level)
- Primary goal: on-prem inference for clinical summarization at ~8-12 reqs/sec (95th perc latency target < 400ms) with local data residency.
- Quality bar: parity with current cloud LLM baseline on our 200-sample clinical prompt set (F1-style eval + human check for hallucinations).
- Constraints: single node initially (A100-class equivalent), then scale to 2 nodes for peak.

Recommended short list for trial (we'll run single-node throughput + quality matrix):
1) Mistral-Instruct-70B (float/FP16 baseline) — highest inference quality per token in our benchmarks.
2) Llama-2-70B-instruct (GPTQ compressed) — strong baseline, familiar for your team.
3) Falcon-40B-instruct (AWQ int4 candidate) — aggressive cost/throughput tradeoff; watch for rare regression on long-context summarization.

Quant/throughput options to evaluate in the matrix
- AWQ int4: best throughput on optimized kernels, risk: subtle token-level regressions in rare cases; lower memory footprint.
- GPTQ int4: more conservative accuracy retention vs AWQ on some instruction tasks; slightly slower but more stable.
- FP8 (mixed bfloat/float8 path): higher accuracy retention, faster than FP16 on some kernels but needs validated runtime support and memory headroom.

Proposed eval matrix (short):
- Models x Quantization (FP16, GPTQ-int4, AWQ-int4, FP8 if supported) x Promptset (PACE-CLIN-200) x 2 sequence lengths (512/2048)
- Metrics: macro-F1/ROUGE, hallucination rate (human spot-check on top 20 failures), median & 95th token latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and memory headroom.

Deliverables we can turn around in 7 business days if we get access:
- Benchmark CSV (pace-benchmarks-v1.csv) with raw latency and quality metrics
- Filtered promptset we used (pace-promptset-v1.jsonl)
- A short trade-off note summarizing AWQ vs GPTQ vs FP8 on your workload (awq-gptq-fp8-tradeoffs-notes.pdf)

Next steps / asks from PaceHealth:
- Grant a short-lived SSO/service account for a sandbox cluster (read-only model pulls) or provide a small test VM image we can run the agent on.
- Confirm target latency SLO and any additional redlines for hallucinations (e.g., maximum 2% critical hallucination rate).
- If acceptable, sign the eval NDA send via DocuSign (I can re-send link).

I cc'd Ben (solutions eng) and Marissa (inference research) who will run the quant/throughput analysis and own the tradeoff notes.

Thanks — I'll queue the job as soon as we have access.

—
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0133

From: Ellie Shaw <ellie@pacehealth.ai>

Jonas —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few quick answers and clarifications inline.

> Primary goal: on-prem inference for clinical summarization at ~8-12 reqs/sec (95th perc latency target < 400ms)
That matches our internal target. We can provision a single node equivalent to an A100-80GB for the test.

> Quality bar: parity with current cloud LLM baseline on our 200-sample clinical prompt set
We'd like to de-risk hallucinations aggressively. If you see >1.5% critical hallucination rate on the sample set we won't move forward with that config.

Access: I can provision a service account for a 3-day window and will upload the sample promptset to the shared Drive folder you listed.

Questions: 1) On FP8 — do you have a runtime we recommend for the test, or will you run FP8 in an experimental branch? 2) For the human spot-check, can you define "critical hallucination" with 2-3 examples we can align on?

Available next week for a short sync on Tuesday morning PST if you want to walk through the matrix before we start.

Thanks,
Ellie
Ellie Shaw
Director, Data Products — PaceHealth
ellie@pacehealth.ai | +1 646-555-0192

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ellie Shaw <ellie@pacehealth.ai>
Date: 2027-06-22T18:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: PaceHealth model suitability & quant plan

Thanks for the summary, Jonas. Adding a few concrete notes on the quant tradeoffs and proposed test knobs — happy to run the full matrix once Ellie provides the sandbox.

Short guidance (practical):
- AWQ (int4): expect ~2.5-3x token/sec improvement vs FP16 on a single A100-like node for 70B models when kernels are optimized; memory footprint reduces enough that 70B AWQ often fits in a single 80GB card. Risk: tail-case degradation on long instruction-style prompts (we've seen a ~1.0-1.8% delta in ROUGE on some clinical summarization promptsets).

- GPTQ (int4): slightly lower throughput (~2.0-2.4x), but typically preserves more fidelity on instruction-following tasks. If hallucination risk is a hard constraint (<1.5% critical), GPTQ is usually safer than AWQ.

- FP8: on runtimes with robust FP8 kernels (we can run on our internal branch), FP8 keeps most FP16 quality while providing throughput improvements (1.3-1.6x) and better numeric stability than int4. Caveat: FP8 rollout requires the runtime binary and careful kernel selection — we should vendor-test it in the sandbox before trusting it for production.

Concrete test matrix we recommend to start (low-cost sweep):
- Model: Mistral-70B, Llama2-70B, Falcon-40B
- Quant: FP16 baseline, GPTQ-int4, AWQ-int4 (Falcon), FP8 (if runtime available)
- Sequences: 512 and 2048 tokens (reflects short & long summaries)
- Runs: 100 samples each cell for automated metrics + 20 human spot-checks on the combined worst-10 failures per cell

Acceptance heuristics (proposal):
- Median latency < 200ms, 95th < 400ms for two-thirds of workload cells
- Critical hallucination rate <= 1.5% on human spot-checks
- Quality delta vs cloud baseline <= 2.5 ROUGE points on average for clinical prompts

Operational notes:
- We'll push a small runner to the Drive folder (redwood-eval-runner.sh) that runs the suite and produces pace-benchmarks-v1.csv. Please allow the service account scp/read on the sandbox VM.
- If AWQ shows a high delta on long-context tests, we recommend a hybrid: AWQ for short summaries and FP16/FP8 for long-context requests with smart routing in Redwood (based on sequence length).

I'll start the internal job as soon as Jonas shares credentials. Ben — can you prep the runner container and include the AWQ/GPTQ versions we tested (tags in the notes PDF)?

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Research Engineer, Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
